summary: Help desk staff handle password reset requests from phone or portal by first logging a ticket, then verifying the caller with their employee ID and security question answer. If verification fails, no reset is done; the caller is told to come to the desk in person with a badge, the ticket is put on hold with the note "ID not verified", and if they failed 3 times in one call the account is also flagged to Security, which closes our part. If verified, the agent checks whether the account is expired or locked: locked accounts are unlocked in the admin console first, and then in both cases the self-service reset link is sent to the registered mobile. The agent waits until the caller confirms they can log in, then closes the ticket with a one-line summary.

summary: When a truck arrives, the driver's paperwork is checked against the open PO list. The driver gets their copy, the PO is received in the system using actual quantities, putaway labels are applied, and pallets are moved out of staging for the putaway crew.

E --> F["Authorize one 30-day bridge supply"]
F --> G

H --> I{Routine med on protocol?}

I -->|"No (controlled substance or not on protocol)"| K["RN routes to prescribing provider inbox for sign-off"]
K --> L{Provider decision}
L -->|Approves| M["Provider e-sends to pharmacy"]
L -->|Denies| N["Request denied"]
K --> O{Still unactioned after 2 business days?}
O -->|Yes| P["RN escalates to covering provider for that day"]
O -->|No| L

M --> Q
N --> Q
Q --> R["Close request in queue"]
summary: Refill requests arrive via the patient portal or phone line and are logged in the refill queue, then staff check the chart for the patient's last visit. If the patient was seen within 12 months, the request goes to the nurse refill pool; if not, staff call the patient to book a follow-up and may authorize one 30-day bridge supply, which still goes through the nurse pool. The RN checks the med against the clinic protocol: routine protocol meds are approved and e-sent by the RN, while controlled substances or off-protocol meds go to the prescribing provider for approval or denial, with escalation to the covering provider if the item sits more than 2 business days. Finally, the patient is told the outcome and the request is closed in the queue.

summary: Each Monday morning, the Reorder Point report is pulled from the ERP and each listed SKU is checked against open POs. After sending the PO, the supplier acknowledgment is chased through a follow-up email and a call, with cancel and re-place with the backup supplier if no date is confirmed. Late ship dates (more than 5 business days past need) trigger an expedite request, with a shortage watch list and sales ops heads-up if refused. Finally, the ERP is updated, the inbound list goes to receiving, and the ack PDF is saved.

summary: This process handles returning a defective lot to a supplier (RTV) after QC flags it. The lot must be on QC HOLD in the WMS before anything starts. An RMA is requested from the supplier, with escalation to the account manager after 3 business days of silence and a handoff to the procurement manager after another 3 days. Key decisions are partial vs full RMA approval, credit vs replacement (with expedited advance replacement for production-critical parts), whether the RTV value exceeds $2,500 (requiring photos and finance approval), and which carrier and freight terms to use. After shipping, inventory is adjusted in the WMS, the credit memo or replacement receipt is tracked (AP deducts an overdue credit after 30 days), and the ticket is closed.

summary: Hardship fund applications arrive in the portal queue and are worked oldest first, with URGENT cases (eviction notice or utility shutoff within 72 hours) taken first. Every case starts with an enrollment check (at least half-time this term); failing it means a denial. Urgent cases can get up to $300 approved the same day and sent to the Bursar before docs arrive, while others get a prior-award check and a documents check (5 business days, one reminder with 3 more, then closed as incomplete). Once docs are complete, prior-award cases go to the Dean of Students director (combined cap $1,500), awards of $750 or less are approved by the coordinator, and larger ones go to the committee for full approval, partial approval, or denial. Approved amounts are checked by Financial Aid against cost of attendance, then the award email and Bursar disbursement form are completed (balance first, unless tagged housing/food emergency), and every case ends with logging in the fund tracker and closing it in the portal.
